newsitem.title: ROMANIA: TABLE - Romania's trade deficit narrows in May.
newsitem.headline: TABLE - Romania's trade deficit narrows in May.

text.p: Romania's trade deficit narrowed to $36 million in May from $94.3 million the previous month, as exports recovered and imports fell further, National Statistics Board (CNS) data showed on Tuesday.

NOTES -- Previous data in brackets. All figures in FOB prices. The CNS said five-month imports this year included $79.6 million of oil imports on which customs documents were delayed. The 1997 data are subject to revisions.
It said exports were 0.3 percent up to $3.36 billion over January-May from the equivalent period of 1996, with textiles and steel products topping the export list.
Five-month imports dropped by 10.5 percent from the same period of 1996, helping the trade deficit to shrink to $339.9 million over January-May from $783.1 million a year ago.
The private sector accounted for 53.4 pecent of exports and 50.1 percent of imports over January-May.
Italy took the bulk of Romanian exports over January-May, when Germany provided most of Romania's imports.
The CNS also said Romania's imports from Japan rose sharply in May, amounting to $70.8 million compared with only $19.6 million in the first four months of this year.
